title: introduce-tenant-geo-blindness-protector-and-kms-claim-mapper
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds tenant geo-blindness enforcement for operator roles, a KMS claim mapper to attach region residency claims to encryption metadata, audit enrichment for residency tags, and an RBAC v2 policy module to enforce region-pinned access. Backfill migration provided for existing audit entries.
description:
Motivation: Tighten the separation between tenant residency metadata and operator-level privileges while preserving necessary operational workflows. This PR implements a 'geo-blindness protector' layer that prevents operator principals from observing tenant geographic residency unless explicitly authorized, and introduces a KMS claim mapper to propagate and enforce residency claims at encryption/decryption time.

Summary of changes: Adds an RBAC v2 policy plugin that evaluates operator tokens against tenant residency claims and denies access when the operator is not allowed to view or act on region-pinned tenants; introduces pkg/kms/claim_mapper which attaches and validates a residency claim to KMS envelope metadata; enriches audit logging with residency_tag and residency_evidence fields so compliance teams can trace decisions; provides a migration tool to backfill residency_tag for historical audit rows based on key usage heuristics; updates the policy compiler with residency-aware predicates and a new operator_scope template; includes unit and integration tests and example policies.

Checklist: 
- [x] RBAC v2 policy module + unit tests
- [x] KMS claim mapper + integration tests (simulated KMS in CI)
- [x] Audit enrichment + backfill migration script
- [x] Policy compiler templates and docs snippets
- [x] E2E regression tests for operator workflows
- [x] Performance baseline (no >2% p95 latency regression on token validation)

Notes on scope and risk: The residency claim is an opaque assertion (string tag + evidence hash) carried in the KMS envelope metadata. The claim_mapper enforces that decryption requires a residency-scope permit when the envelope has a residency_tag and the requesting principal lacks a residency grant. Operator workflows that previously used raw key access will receive denials unless explicitly granted via the new operator-scoped policy template. Migration will backfill audit entries but does not change ciphertexts; operators should coordinate unlock windows with customer success for high-impact tenants.

Rollout plan: Canary the new RBAC predicate on a small operator cohort (internal-ops) for 48 hours with audit-only mode enabled. If metrics look good, flip hard deny for the rest of the fleet. Migration script run during maintenance window.
